maximum_permitted_stay: Up to 3 months initially; extension up to 60 days in two intervals.
passport_validity_rule: At least 6 months from intended arrival.
blank_passport_pages_rule: No minimum blank-page count stated in the current NCIC tourist checklist.
return_ticket_rule: Travel itinerary or booking required; a separate return-ticket document is not specified.
proof_of_funds_rule: No fixed proof-of-funds item in the tourist checklist; additional documents may be requested.
accommodation_rule: Hotel booking or reservation; if using other accommodation, provide the address.
travel_insurance_rule: Not specified in the reviewed official tourist-visa guidance.
yellow_fever_or_health_rule: Yellow-fever vaccination certificate no longer mandatory for entry since 2 October 2026, per NCIC notice; older wording is superseded.
transit_rule: Separate online transit visa for transit to a third country: maximum 7 days, non-extendable, USD50; no Bangladesh-specific airside exemption verified.
application_channel: Official online portal; approval letter required before travel; no visa on arrival; biometric capture at immigration office/border after approval.
application_fee: USD 50; non-refundable; payment subject to a bank charge.
processing_time: Decision within 2–3 days per NCIC notice; apply at least 10 days ahead; estimate, not guarantee.
required_documents: Passport biodata page copy with at least 6 months validity|Tour plan|Travel itinerary or booking|Recent passport-size photograph|Hotel booking or reservation or other accommodation address|Documents in English|Additional documents if requested
review_notes: Bangladesh is absent from the current NCIC visa-exempt nationality list. Visa-prone travellers must apply online and obtain travel authorisation/approval before departure; NCIC says no visas are issued on arrival. The single-entry tourist visa may be granted for up to three months; the approval authorisation itself expires 90 days after approval. Government fee USD50, non-refundable and subject to bank charge. The NCIC notice states a 2–3 day decision period and advises applying at least ten days before travel; this is not a guarantee. The current tourist checklist requires a passport biodata copy with six months validity, tour plan, itinerary/booking, recent passport-size photo and accommodation booking/address. The 2 October 2026 NCIC notice removes the previously stated yellow-fever certificate requirement for entry. A separate transit visa is available for up to seven days. Biometric capture occurs at an immigration office/border after approval and is not a substitute for the uploaded photograph.

review_notes: The official Category C page explicitly lists Bangladesh and requires applicants to apply, pay online and obtain a visa before travelling. The official eVisa FAQ gives an average processing time of seven working days, advises applying at least three weeks before travel, and says a single-entry eVisa is valid for three months from issue. That three-month period is the entry-validity window, not a published initial stay duration. The entry officer sets the stay period; the published Immigration Regulations state that a visitor may not remain beyond six months without Chief Immigration Officer permission. The official fee schedule lists USD30 for an ordinary single-entry online visa, but the eVisa FAQ reserves the Department's right to change visa type and fee during processing. The holiday checklist requires passport photo, biodata scan, proof of residence and destination address; host invitation and host residence/ID are required if staying with a resident. The Regulations permit an officer to request evidence of sufficient means and readmission. The reviewed official checklist does not state numeric passport validity or photo dimensions.
